basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Sits between a product family or catalog item and a physical item: one resolved set of feature choices, not the whole option space.
Holds nominal properties of the configured definition, not measured values of a built unit.
Differs from an engineering BOM: it records selected features and rule results, while the BOM records component occurrences.
Differs from a configuration session, offer or order: those are transactions that may reference a released variant.

may: Resolve the product family and aliases before reading a variant.
Explain which selections, inherited values and rules produced a variant.
Request a feasibility check from an approved evaluator and store its verdict.
Compare variants and report differences in features and nominal properties.
mustNot: Declare a configuration buildable or safe without a retained evaluator verdict.
Infer physical limits, materials or certifications from the product class name.
Execute imported rule code from an external configurator.
Disclose customer-specific or confidential configurations without authority.
Release or retire a variant that existing items still depend on without continuity handling.
requiresHuman: Releasing a variant as a reusable baseline.
Accepting a configuration that a rule marks as an exception.

considerations: Wrong nominal properties for a variant can reach buyers as safety or capacity claims.
Customer-specific configurations can reveal private needs, such as accessibility or medical adaptations.
Hidden option rules can steer buyers to costlier variants without explanation.
affectedParties: Buyers and users of the configured product
Engineers and release authorities accountable for the definition
Service and repair staff who rely on the variant record

items: A variant is identified by its family reference plus a resolved set of feature values and a revision.
Physical units are matched to it through model or part number, serial plate and configuration code.
Confused with the product type, the individual item, a configuration session and an order line.
Building or shipping an infeasible or unvalidated combination.
Spare parts or service instructions applied to the wrong variant.
Stale effectivity causing a superseded variant to be sold or built.
ISO 10303-242 (STEP AP242) for configured product structure.
GS1 GTIN for trade item variants.
Nominal mass in kilograms, stated as unloaded or operating mass.
Nominal overall dimensions in millimetres, with the reference orientation stated.
Rated electrical, mechanical or thermal capacity in SI units, with the rating standard stated.
Operating environment limits such as temperature range in degrees Celsius.
Material and finish designations by referenced classification.
Source and evidence for each value, marked as nominal rather than measured.
